overview: This file documents a two-year effort by the American Consulate at Dairen to obtain United States publications, zoning ordinances, city plans, and engineering maps for the Kwantung Government’s redevelopment of Dairen. Governor Takeshita sought American expertise as rapid population growth, construction of a civic center and railroad station, the transfer of the territorial government to Dairen, and plans for “Greater” Dairen created an urgent need for municipal planning. The correspondence traces cooperation among the State Department, Department of Commerce, Bureau of Standards, and National Resources Committee, culminating in the provision of planning literature and recommendations for obtaining maps and reports from several American cities.

subfiles.title: Grummon despatch requesting American city-planning assistance
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Grummon requests American planning and zoning publications to assist the Kwantung Government with Dairen’s rapid expansion.
subfiles.summary: Governor Takeshita asked the United States for assistance with town planning, zoning, and satellite-town planning as Dairen approached a population of half a million and prepared to become the territorial capital. Grummon describes a planned civic center, government housing, and a new railroad station, and requests federal reports and materials from Washington, New York, Philadelphia, Los Angeles, and Westchester. He stresses the diplomatic importance of responding because Sweden and Germany had received similar requests.

subfiles.title: Grummon follow-up requesting two federal planning pamphlets
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Grummon asks that two readily available Department of Commerce pamphlets be sent while the broader collection of planning material is being assembled.
subfiles.summary: Referring to his September 1935 despatch, Grummon identifies “City Planning Primer” and “Preparation of Zoning Ordinances” in a United States Information Service pamphlet. Because the German and Swedish consuls had already answered the Kwantung Government’s inquiries, he requests prompt delivery of these works for transmission to Port Arthur if the complete collection is not yet ready.

subfiles.title: Zapf letter reporting referral to the Bureau of Standards
subfiles.to: Wilbur J. Carr, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Zapf explains that the earlier consular despatch had not reached his section and reports forwarding it to the Bureau of Standards.
subfiles.summary: Zapf states that the Far Eastern Section of the Division of Regional Information had no record or recollection of previously seeing Grummon’s September 1935 report. After receiving the State Department’s original file copy on loan, the section sent it to the Assistant Director of the Bureau of Standards for preparation of the requested information.

subfiles.title: Moser letter transmitting the Dairen request to McAllister
subfiles.from: C. K. Moser, Chief, Far Eastern Section, Division of Regional Information
subfiles.to: A. S. McAllister, Assistant Director, Bureau of Standards
subfiles.about: Moser formally sends the State Department’s original consular despatch to McAllister for consideration.
subfiles.summary: Following a telephone conversation between H. R. Stutman and McAllister, Moser attaches the American consul’s original report concerning Dairen planning. He asks McAllister’s committee to consider the request and emphasizes that the unique State Department file copy must be returned with the reply.

subfiles.title: Zapf letter forwarding Bureau of Standards planning material
subfiles.to: Wilbur J. Carr, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Zapf returns Grummon’s despatch and forwards the Bureau of Standards’ available planning material and procurement advice.
subfiles.summary: Zapf encloses a letter from McAllister, the State Department file copy of Grummon’s despatch, and planning material located by the Bureau of Standards. He notes that four older publications were no longer held by the Bureau but could be purchased from the Superintendent of Documents or possibly obtained from the National Resources Committee, which also had newer planning and zoning material.

subfiles.title: State Department instruction transmitting planning literature to Dairen
subfiles.about: The State Department sends the interdepartmental correspondence and a substantial collection of American planning and zoning publications to Dairen.
subfiles.summary: The instruction responds to Grummon’s despatches of September 1935 and March 1936 by forwarding the Department of Commerce letters and their enclosures. It lists primers, model zoning and city-planning enabling acts, zoning guidance, and National Resources Board references on regional planning, courts, health, cooperation, and national and state planning.

subfiles.title: Grummon despatch requesting engineers’ zoning maps
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Grummon conveys a new Kwantung Government request for practical engineers’ maps of American cities with advanced zoning systems.
subfiles.summary: Grummon thanks the Department for the earlier planning literature, which the Kwantung authorities appreciated. With the territorial government preparing to transfer its headquarters to Dairen and plan “Greater” Dairen, he asks whether engineers’ maps from one or two American cities could be obtained. He suggests approaching municipal planning bodies, the Public Works Administration’s Housing Division, or the Department of Labor’s United States Housing Corporation.

subfiles.title: Delano letter recommending American city plans and zoning maps
subfiles.from: Frederic A. Delano, Vice-Chairman, National Resources Committee
subfiles.about: Delano supplies two planning publications and identifies American cities from which more detailed zoning maps and reports might be obtained.
subfiles.summary: The National Resources Committee provides copies of the Memphis city plan and Nashville building-zone ordinance for forwarding to Grummon. Delano explains the limitations of inexpensive published zoning maps and gives contacts for larger-scale maps or atlases from San Francisco, Akron, and Dayton. He also recommends regional or municipal plans for New York, Cincinnati, and Springfield and describes Nashville’s 1936 ordinance as especially highly regarded.

interest: The file offers a compact case study of technical diplomacy between the United States and the Japanese colonial administration of the Kwantung Leased Territory. It shows both Dairen’s ambitions as a rapidly growing planned capital and the bureaucratic path by which American urban-planning knowledge moved through the State Department, Commerce Department, Bureau of Standards, and National Resources Committee. Particularly useful are the specific publications, map scales, prices, addresses, and municipal contacts, which reveal the practical international circulation of American zoning models during the 1930s.
